note: The Credit and Data Bureau's own pages (cdb.com.pg, read 2026-10-31): its About page says it operates in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands, set up by leading financial institutions. No PNG law or Bank of PNG rule on credit reporting was found (the Bank of PNG's site and PacLII answer with a Cloudflare check; the searches found no Act), so the file rests on the bureau's own statements. FAQ: information stays on the bureau for seven years; it deletes nothing unless inaccurate, and a payment only amends the balance: written as keep 7 (a paid default stays the same seven years). Services page: a debt is in default when unpaid beyond the credit terms, and members generally load debts in default for more than 60 days: written as reported 61 days after the due date ('more than 60 days' is 61); 'generally' is the bureau's word, a practice and not a rule, and the Code of Conduct it names wasn't read.

sources.title: Credit and Data Bureau Ltd: FAQs
sources.said: How long does information stay on the Credit Bureau? ... Information stays on the Credit Bureau for a duration of seven years. The Credit Bureau does not delete any information unless it is inaccurate. If a payment is made towards a debt that is on your file, it will be amended to carry the balance or zero.

sources.title: Credit and Data Bureau Ltd: Services
sources.said: A debt is in default when it is unpaid beyond the credit terms given. Generally members load debts which are in default for more than 60 days.

sources.title: Credit and Data Bureau Ltd: About
sources.said: Established by a number of leading financial institutions and associated groups, Credit & Data Bureau operates in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands.
